reviewed_account1_fields.proposed_claim: In an April 22, 2025 NPR interview, Steven Levitsky said the United States had crossed into “competitive authoritarianism”; this is his assessment, not a verified finding that constitutional government ended.
reviewed_account1_fields.proposed_short: In an April 2025 NPR interview, Steven Levitsky said the U.S. had crossed into “competitive authoritarianism.”
reviewed_account1_fields.proposed_medium: In an April 22, 2025, NPR Fresh Air interview, Harvard political scientist Steven Levitsky said the United States was “no longer living in a democratic regime” and had crossed into “competitive authoritarianism.” He cited government retaliation risks and attacks or threats involving critics and institutions. These statements report Levitsky’s assessment; they do not establish a formal end to constitutional government.
reviewed_account1_fields.proposed_long: NPR’s Fresh Air interviewed Harvard political scientist Steven Levitsky on April 22, 2025, about American democracy under President Donald Trump. Levitsky said that, in his view, the country was “no longer living in a democratic regime” and had crossed into “competitive authoritarianism.” He pointed to what he described as a cost to publicly opposing the government, including attacks or threats involving law firms, company leaders, media, universities, nongovernmental organizations and individual critics. This account attributes those conclusions and examples to Levitsky. The interview supports reporting his assessment of democratic backsliding; it does not establish that all constitutional checks were eliminated, that the republic formally ended, or that permanent autocracy was achieved. The interview does not establish a completed 248-year constitutional collapse. Levitsky also called the situation mild compared with other cases, reversible, and said he was pessimistic in the short term.
